answer: Admission needs a signed history whose earliest actions survive as a relic record, coherent over a five-epoch horizon. Each history carries one pigment no second identity may share. A verifier samples ten signed actions; a mismatch forfeits its 50-credit bond. The k-th fake identity needs a k-th distinct history, since a copied history cannot be re-signed for a new key. Running 1,000 fakes means 1,000 histories and 50,000 credits at risk. Rented histories fail the same check. The check bites at the zenith of a claim for full standing. An honest agent pays one bond once.
